intent: Frame a scrolling message transcript that follows its newest content, keeps anchored messages in view and floats a jump button over its edge.
typical_uses: A conversation transcript that grows at the end while the reader may be scrolled back into its history

dont_use_when.situation: A generic scrollable panel with no following, anchoring or jumping to a message
A list long enough to need windowing, where only the rows in view exist in the DOM

instead.note: Every MessageScrollerItem stays mounted; `content-visibility: auto` in message-scroller.module.css skips rendering work for items off screen but does not remove them. The kit ships no virtualized list.

invariants.text: The frame is a relatively positioned flex column at `height: 100%` that clips its overflow; the viewport scrolls only when its parent gives it a bounded height, which the viewport then fills.

The frame and the viewport both carry `data-scrollable` naming the edges past which more content lies (`start`, `end` or `start end`, absent when neither), and `data-autoscrolling` for a moment after a scroll to the end starts.

good.title: A transcript with a jump-to-end button, inside its provider
good.code:
<MessageScrollerProvider autoScroll>
  <MessageScroller style={{ height: 480 }}>
    <MessageScrollerViewport>
      <MessageScrollerContent>
        {messages.map((message, index) => (
          <MessageScrollerItem
            key={message.id}
            messageId={message.id}
            scrollAnchor={index === messages.length - 1}
          >
            <Message>
              <MessageContent>
                <Bubble>
                  <BubbleContent>{message.text}</BubbleContent>
                </Bubble>
              </MessageContent>
            </Message>
          </MessageScrollerItem>
        ))}
      </MessageScrollerContent>
    </MessageScrollerViewport>
    <MessageScrollerButton direction="end" />
  </MessageScroller>
</MessageScrollerProvider>

bad.title: A scroller rendered without its provider
bad.why: Every part reads the scroller state from a MessageScrollerProvider above it and throws without one; wrap the scroller in the provider.
